quick_skim.title: Evolving Memory, Learning to Meta-Control: Test-Time Adaptation for Experience-augmented LLM Agents
quick_skim.abstract: Self-evolving agents accumulate experience from task streams, but existing frameworks typically rely on fixed pipelines to retrieve and utilize this experience, neglecting when and how to deploy it. We introduce Online Meta-Control of Experience (OMCE), a framework that updates experience memory and learns a meta-control policy from task feedback during test-time adaptation. OMCE employs a lightweight contextual-bandit meta-controller that uses compact retrieval signals to select among four cognitive actions: DIRECT, EPISODE, GUIDE, and DISTILL. This routing mechanism operationalizes three coupled decisions: whether to invoke experience, which memory format to utilize, and when to consolidate new guidance. OMCE evolves online, leveraging task feedback to update the memory bank and refine the routing policy via contextual bandit updates. Experiments on four online adaptation benchmarks across four backbones show that OMCE improves first-attempt success by up to 20.5 percentage points over the strongest compared baseline, while reducing per-task token use by a factor of 5.7 to 62.5 relative to ACE with GPT-5.2. Controlled ablations further support the benefits of learned routing and continued routing policy adaptation.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: experience memory updating and retrieval control for LLM agents

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Self-evolving LLM agents store experience but use fixed retrieval pipelines. This paper proposes OMCE, which updates experience memory online and learns a contextual-bandit meta-controller that routes compact retrieval signals to four cognitive actions, deciding when and how to reuse experience.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 现有自演化智能体虽能积累经验，却依赖固定流水线检索经验，忽视了何时以及如何调用。作者提出在线经验元控制框架OMCE，在测试时自适应中持续更新经验记忆，并用轻量上下文赌博机元控制器依据紧凑检索信号在DIRECT、EPISODE、GUIDE、DISTILL四种认知动作间路由。该机制同时决定是否调用经验、使用何种记忆格式以及何时固化新指导，使经验检索从静态流程变为可学习的决策过程。其意义在于为智能体长期记忆的按需调用提供了可训练的控制范式。

quick_skim.title: Learning by Doing: Autonomously Compiling and Curating Agent Skills from Verified Traces
quick_skim.abstract: Memory systems for production LLM agents mostly store semantic memory (facts about users and domains) or episodic memory (earlier interactions). Research systems such as Trace2Skill, WikiSkill, and SkillRevise learn procedures from agent runs, package them as Skills, and evaluate them on benchmarks. We describe Zep Agent Skills, a production service that gives deployed agents this procedural memory. The service uses only verified attempts as evidence, cites the supporting events for each field of a Skill, and governs the admission and distribution of each Skill version. The service records each task attempt as a Trace with ordered events, an outcome, and a verification strength. A compiler with separate Reflector and Curator roles turns verified Traces into versioned Skills. Scans and admission gates control which candidates become active, and verified use outcomes change the search rank of each Skill. The Agent Skills format is an open standard that Anthropic originated and donated to the Agentic AI Foundation, so any host of the format can load a compiled Skill. Agents retrieve Skills through lexical search with progressive disclosure, over an API or MCP. We evaluate Zep Agent Skills on $τ^3$-bench banking, AppWorld, and EnterpriseOps-Gym. Skills compiled from the Traces of a teacher model increase the pass rate of three weaker executor models on the same tasks, at every reasoning effort, by 4.5 to 18.8 points. Most of the gain is on the tasks that the teacher solved. On ALFWorld, Skills compiled from the runs of a small model give a gain similar to or larger than the gain that prior work reports for continuous fine-tuning, with no training.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: procedural memory service for deployed LLM agents
quick_skim.llm_evidence_cn: 面向已部署LLM智能体的程序性记忆服务

quick_skim.title: Scalaris: A Scalable Enterprise Memory Architecture for Conversational AI Assistants
quick_skim.abstract: Enterprise conversational systems require memory to personalize interactions, retain information across sessions, and maintain conversational coherence. At enterprise scale, however, memory must not only retrieve relevant information accurately but also provide it efficiently to the answer-generation model. Existing memory systems face a trade-off between retrieval accuracy and context efficiency. Retrieving more context can improve recall but increases inference cost and latency. We present Scalaris, a scalable enterprise memory architecture that addresses this trade-off through a unified long-term and short-term memory design. We propose that user interactions and assistant responses possess distinct characteristics and roles in a conversation: user interactions capture evolving knowledge about the user and provide value across sessions, whereas assistant responses must be stored efficiently so that only information relevant to the current query is retrieved. We therefore treat them separately and support each with specialized representations and ingestion/retrieval pipelines. Scalaris reaches 92.2 % accuracy on LongMemEval-S and 90.77 % on LoCoMo using Qwen3-32B, state-of-the-art results on both benchmarks, while supplying the answer-generation model with approximately 10 times fewer retrieved context tokens than Hindsight, a leading memory system for conversational AI. When integrated with our proprietary closed-source AI assistants, Scalaris improved overall response quality by 36 %. Together, these results establish Scalaris as a cost-effective framework for building scalable, personalized conversational AI systems.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: Unified long-term and short-term memory architecture for conversational AI assistants with efficient retrieval

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Enterprise conversational assistants need memory that is both accurate and context-efficient. Scalaris proposes a unified long-term and short-term memory architecture that balances retrieval accuracy against inference cost and latency at enterprise scale.

quick_skim.title: Twists and Turns: A Graph-Based Benchmark and Framework for Long-Term Memory in Exploration Tasks
quick_skim.abstract: Long-term problem-solving processes, such as scientific research and software development, proceed along an evolving trial-and-error trajectory toward a central goal. We term these \textit{exploration tasks}, which require models to remember not only facts but also how solutions are tested against intermediate outcomes and early attempts are continually revised or revived. However, existing long-term memory research focuses on factual recall and updates, overlooking the interconnected nature of exploration. We observe that exploration processes naturally form graphs, with branching approaches linked by revisions and reconsiderations. Motivated by this, we propose \textsc{LExMem}, a graph-guided benchmark designed to evaluate \underline{\textsc{Mem}}ory in \underline{\textsc{L}}ong-term \underline{\textsc{Ex}}ploration tasks. We model exploration processes as graphs and introduce an evolutionary mechanism to increase their structural complexity, yielding 224 dialogues and 2,018 question-answer instances derived from graph structures. Building on the same insight, we propose \textsc{LExGraph}, a graph-based memory framework that incrementally organizes dialogues into interconnected memory nodes and retrieves evidence through hybrid retrieval and neighbor expansion. Extensive experiments demonstrate that \textsc{LExMem} poses a significant challenge to existing retrieval- and memory-based systems, whereas \textsc{LExGraph} achieves superior performance and generalizes effectively to external benchmarks. Codes and datasets are available at https://github.com/mbzuai-nlp/LExMem.

quick_skim.title: A State Change Is Local, Its Consequences Are Not: Dependency-Aware State Revision for Long-Term Agent Memory
quick_skim.abstract: Long-lived agents rely on persistent memory of users, tasks and decisions, and this memory must stay consistent with a world that keeps changing. When an upstream fact changes, however, memory systems can revise the contradicted memory itself while the beliefs, plans and actions derived from it remain accepted, even though they have lost their support. We therefore formulate dependency-aware state revision, which asks not only what changed but also which dependent states should no longer be trusted. To address it, StateGraph maintains an evolving state dependency graph whose edges are recovered from interaction histories. Its core design is counterfactual verification: each candidate edge is tested by asking whether the dependent state would survive the loss of its premise, which separates support dependence from semantic relatedness, and revision then invalidates a dependent state only when a strict dependency fails and no independent support path survives. To test this design, we introduce StateChangeBench, a controlled benchmark of 50 author-constructed cases annotated with cascade depth, hard negatives and action consequences. On it, StateGraph's Impact-F1 margin over a CUPMem reimplementation is 6.9 percentage points at depth 1 and 26.0 at depth 3+. On public long-term memory benchmarks, its point estimates are comparable to or higher than those of the evaluated baselines on most datasets. These results provide initial evidence that explicit dependency tracking can improve selective memory revision under changing conditions.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: dependency-aware state revision for persistent long-term agent memory

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Long-lived agents keep persistent memory, yet when an upstream fact changes, derived beliefs and plans silently lose support. StateGraph recovers a state dependency graph from interaction histories and applies counterfactual verification to decide which dependent states should be revised.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 长期运行的智能体依赖持久记忆，但当上游事实改变时，记忆系统往往只修正被直接矛盾的那条记忆，而由它推导出的信念、计划与行动仍被保留，失去支撑却未被清理。作者据此提出依赖感知的状态修订问题，并构建StateGraph：从交互历史中恢复状态依赖图的边，用反事实验证逐一检验候选依赖关系，判断哪些派生状态应不再可信。该工作把记忆维护从单点更新扩展为依赖传播，为长期智能体记忆的一致性提供了新框架。

quick_skim.title: Prospective Memory for Proactive LLM Agents
quick_skim.abstract: Most memory systems for LLM agents are retrospective, preserving and retrieving past information to inform current decisions. Proactive agents, however, also require prospective memory: retaining future-directed intentions and realizing them when appropriate opportunities arise, even without explicit requests. Crucially, remembering the right intention does not guarantee acting at the right time: a related observation may call for waiting, while a later cue may make the same intention actionable. Inspired by cognitive theories of human prospective memory, we introduce Pro-Memory, a memory framework that separates maintaining future intentions from deciding when and how to realize them. Pro-Memory preserves pending objectives linked to their supporting evidence, assesses new observations against their original goals and activation conditions, and coordinates appropriate contributions with the agent's ongoing actions. It further updates intention states based on actions actually issued or evidence of resolution, while an experience memory distills feedback from completed episodes into guidance for future decisions. Experiments on two benchmarks spanning delayed-intention tasks and open-ended proactive assistance demonstrate consistent improvements in proactive task performance over representative memory approaches across multiple LLM backbones, while limiting unnecessary interventions.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: memory framework for LLM agents storing future intentions
quick_skim.llm_evidence_cn: 面向LLM智能体的记忆框架，保存未来意图

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Existing LLM agent memory systems only look backward. Pro-Memory adds prospective memory, keeping future-directed intentions tied to supporting evidence and deciding when a cue makes them actionable, separating retention from timely realization.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 现有LLM智能体的记忆系统大多是回溯式的，只保存和检索过去信息，难以支撑需要主动性的智能体。作者受人类前瞻记忆认知理论启发，提出Pro-Memory框架，将未来意图的维持与何时、如何执行该意图的决策分离，并让待办目标与支撑证据相绑定。该框架在新观测到来时评估其是否构成合适的行动时机，从而避免过早或过晚触发。其贡献在于为智能体记忆补充了前瞻性维度，使主动式代理能够在恰当机会出现时自主实现既定意图。
